appraisal_events.evidence: il s'imaginait qu'Odette était la maîtresse de Forcheville... elle avait dû avoir... les mêmes regards brillants, malicieux, abaissés et sournois, que le jour où celui-ci avait chassé Saniette; « Mais aussi, je suis trop bête... je paie avec mon argent le plaisir des autres. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Driven by jealous fantasy, Swann accuses Odette of mocking him in complicity with Forcheville and resents having financed her pleasures; the narrator explicitly frames this as Swann's own 'imaginations mauvaises,' so the accusation carries ironic distance rather than confirmed narrative fact.

appraisal_events.evidence: Elle lui écrivit que les Verdurin et leurs amis avaient manifesté le désir d'assister à ces représentations de Wagner... De lui, elle ne disait pas un mot, il était sous-entendu que leur présence excluait la sienne.
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette's actual letter asks Swann only for money to host the Verdurin circle and Forcheville, never mentioning him at all; the narrator states plainly that his own presence was implicitly excluded, a direct social snub distinct from Swann's earlier fantasy.

status_effects.explanation: In Swann's jealous construction Odette is diminished as complicit, mocking, and mercenary, though the passage flags this reading as his own invention rather than settled fact.
Swann's hatred and suspicion intensify, consuming him with vindictive fantasies even as he savors imagined revenge, marking a worsened local emotional state.
Swann is explicitly left out of Odette's planned gathering with the Verdurins and Forcheville, reduced to the role of financier while excluded from the event itself.

ambiguities: Odette's diminishment in E1 is explicitly framed as Swann's own paranoid fantasy ('ses imaginations mauvaises'), not confirmed narrative fact; the passage closes by noting this hateful image later fades into a tender image of Odette confiding in and trusting Swann, so her local diminishment should be read as unstable and cyclical rather than settled.
